verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own docs describe a first-party custom URI protocol (Obsidian URI) that triggers actions such as opening a note or creating a note. That directly covers the story's "URI scheme" path for driving the app from scripts. missing for 10: detail on URI actions and parameters (e.g. vault/file targeting, content injection), any documented local HTTP endpoint, and independent or hands-on corroboration of URI-driven automation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the app from outside — create or open notes via a URI scheme, deep links, or a local endpoint — to wire it into my scripts and workflows

citations.quote: Obsidian URI is a custom URI protocol supported by Obsidian that lets you trigger various actions, such as opening a note or creating a note.
